_comment: Asherman's syndrome is acquired/structural, not monogenic - no Disease-associates-Gene edge is added. Modeled instead via Disease-localizes-Anatomy and Disease-presents-Symptom edges, using Hetionet's real metaedge for disease-anatomy relationships (DlA, 'localizes') rather than a generic 'associates' label, since Hetionet has no Disease-associates-Anatomy metaedge. No approved pharmacological treatment exists (management is surgical, e.g. hysteroscopic adhesiolysis), so no Compound-treats-Disease edge either. This node is legitimately sparser than the others.

node.name: Asherman's syndrome
node.notes: Acquired condition: intrauterine adhesions/fibrosis, typically following uterine surgery (e.g. dilation and curettage) or infection. Not a primarily genetic disease and has no single causal gene. Not present in Hetionet v1.0's 137-disease set.

supporting_nodes.name: uterus
supporting_nodes.notes: Reused directly from Hetionet v1.0 (already present as UBERON:0000995).

supporting_nodes.name: endometrium
supporting_nodes.notes: Reused directly from Hetionet v1.0 (already present as UBERON:0001295). Primary site of the intrauterine adhesions/scarring.

supporting_nodes.name: Infertility
supporting_nodes.notes: Not present in Hetionet v1.0's 438-symptom MeSH-derived set. Common presenting symptom of Asherman's syndrome due to obliteration of the endometrial cavity.

supporting_nodes.name: Amenorrhea
supporting_nodes.notes: Not present in Hetionet v1.0's 438-symptom MeSH-derived set (closest existing term is Symptom::D004412 Dysmenorrhea, which is distinct). Common presenting symptom of Asherman's syndrome, particularly with severe adhesions.

edges.evidence: Asherman's syndrome is defined by intrauterine adhesions within the uterine cavity.
The adhesions/fibrosis characteristic of Asherman's syndrome form on and replace the functional endometrial lining.
Infertility is a leading presenting complaint in Asherman's syndrome, due to impaired implantation and endometrial cavity distortion.
Hypomenorrhea/amenorrhea is a classic presenting symptom, especially in moderate-to-severe cases.

deliberately_omitted.disease_associates_gene: Asherman's syndrome is an acquired, structural condition (post-surgical/infectious intrauterine scarring), not a monogenic or strongly polygenic disease - no defensible single-gene association exists to cite.
deliberately_omitted.compound_treats_disease: No approved pharmacological treatment exists. Standard of care is surgical (hysteroscopic adhesiolysis), sometimes with post-operative estrogen to promote re-epithelialization - not a disease-modifying compound therapy in the sense Hetionet's CtD edges represent.
